<!doctype html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
<meta charset="utf-8">
<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width,initial-scale=1">
<title>Math Careers: Five-Minute Challenges</title>
<style>
  :root{--ink:#18253b;--muted:#52627a;--paper:#f5f8fc;--card:#fff;--blue:#315ee8;--line:#dce4ef;--green:#087653;--red:#a43a35}
  *{box-sizing:border-box}
  body{margin:0;background:var(--paper);color:var(--ink);font:16px/1.5 system-ui,-apple-system,Segoe UI,sans-serif}
  main{max-width:920px;margin:auto;padding:28px 18px 48px}
  h1{font-size:clamp(1.7rem,4vw,2.4rem);line-height:1.15;margin:0 0 8px}
  .intro{color:var(--muted);margin:0 0 22px}
  .tabs{display:grid;grid-template-columns:repeat(4,1fr);gap:8px;margin-bottom:16px}
  button,select,input{font:inherit}
  .tab{border:1px solid var(--line);border-radius:12px;background:#fff;color:var(--ink);padding:11px 8px;cursor:pointer;font-weight:700}
  .tab[aria-selected="true"]{background:var(--blue);border-color:var(--blue);color:#fff}
  .card{background:var(--card);border:1px solid var(--line);border-radius:18px;padding:clamp(18px,4vw,30px);box-shadow:0 8px 24px #1b31520b}
  .topline{display:flex;justify-content:space-between;align-items:center;gap:12px;flex-wrap:wrap}
  .badge{font-size:.82rem;background:#edf2ff;color:#2647b9;padding:5px 10px;border-radius:99px;font-weight:700}
  .timer{font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums;font-size:1.15rem;font-weight:800}
  h2{font-size:1.55rem;margin:14px 0 3px}
  .role{color:var(--muted);margin:0 0 17px}
  .scenario{background:#f2f6fc;border-left:4px solid var(--blue);padding:13px 15px;border-radius:8px;margin:15px 0}
  .steps{padding-left:22px}
  .steps li{margin:6px 0}
  .formrow{display:flex;gap:10px;align-items:center;flex-wrap:wrap;margin:14px 0}
  input,select{border:1px solid #bdc9da;border-radius:9px;padding:10px 12px;background:#fff;color:var(--ink);max-width:100%}
  input[type="number"]{width:110px}
  .action{border:0;border-radius:9px;background:var(--blue);color:#fff;padding:10px 15px;font-weight:750;cursor:pointer}
  .action.secondary{background:#e9eef8;color:var(--ink)}
  .action:hover,.tab:hover{filter:brightness(.96)}
  .feedback{min-height:28px;margin:10px 0 0;font-weight:700}
  .good{color:var(--green)} .try{color:var(--red)}
  .stretch{border-top:1px solid var(--line);padding-top:14px;margin-top:20px}
  .stretch strong{color:#253b70}
  .hint{color:var(--muted);font-size:.93rem}
  .footer{color:var(--muted);font-size:.9rem;margin-top:14px}
  @media(max-width:620px){.tabs{grid-template-columns:repeat(2,1fr)}}
</style>
</head>
<body>
<main>
  <h1>Math Careers: Five-Minute Challenges</h1>
  <p class="intro">Choose a career, start the timer, and try a small piece of the work. You can switch activities any time.</p>
  <div class="tabs" role="tablist" aria-label="Math career activities">
    <button class="tab" role="tab" aria-selected="true" data-panel="teach">Math Teaching</button>
    <button class="tab" role="tab" aria-selected="false" data-panel="pure">Pure Math</button>
    <button class="tab" role="tab" aria-selected="false" data-panel="applied">Applied Math</button>
    <button class="tab" role="tab" aria-selected="false" data-panel="data">Statistics &amp; Data Science</button>
  </div>

  <section class="card panel" id="teach" role="tabpanel">
    <div class="topline"><span class="badge">Explain an idea clearly</span><span class="timer" id="timer-teach">05:00</span></div>
    <h2>Math Teaching</h2>
    <p class="role">Math teachers help people make sense of ideas and find ways through confusion.</p>
    <div class="scenario"><strong>Your student says:</strong> “I know 3 × 4 is 12, but I don’t understand why.” Help them see what multiplication means.</div>
    <ol class="steps">
      <li>Choose a model: equal groups, an array, or a number line.</li>
      <li>Sketch it or describe it in one or two sentences.</li>
      <li>Ask a question that would help you check the student’s understanding.</li>
    </ol>
    <div class="formrow">
      <label for="teach-model">I’ll use</label>
      <select id="teach-model"><option>4 groups of 3 objects</option><option>3 rows of 4 dots</option><option>3 jumps of 4 on a number line</option></select>
      <button class="action" onclick="checkTeach()">Reveal a sample</button>
    </div>
    <p class="feedback" id="feedback-teach" aria-live="polite"></p>
    <div class="stretch"><strong>Stretch for grades 9–12:</strong> A student says, “If you multiply by a fraction, the answer always gets bigger.” Write a counterexample and a question that could guide them to notice the pattern.</div>
  </section>

  <section class="card panel" id="pure" role="tabpanel" hidden>
    <div class="topline"><span class="badge">Spot a pattern and test it</span><span class="timer" id="timer-pure">05:00</span></div>
    <h2>Pure Math</h2>
    <p class="role">Pure mathematicians explore patterns, structures, and why mathematical statements are true.</p>
    <div class="scenario"><strong>Explore:</strong> Look at the first few square numbers: 1, 4, 9, 16, 25… Compare each one with the square before it.</div>
    <ol class="steps">
      <li>Find the differences between neighboring squares.</li>
      <li>Predict the next difference and the next square number.</li>
      <li>Try to explain why the differences follow that pattern.</li>
    </ol>
    <div class="formrow">
      <label for="pure-answer">Next difference:</label><input type="number" id="pure-answer" placeholder="e.g. 11">
      <button class="action" onclick="checkPure()">Check</button>
    </div>
    <p class="feedback" id="feedback-pure" aria-live="polite"></p>
    <div class="stretch"><strong>Stretch for grades 9–12:</strong> Use (n + 1)² − n² to explain why the differences between consecutive square numbers are consecutive odd numbers.</div>
  </section>

  <section class="card panel" id="applied" role="tabpanel" hidden>
    <div class="topline"><span class="badge">Use math to solve a real problem</span><span class="timer" id="timer-applied">05:00</span></div>
    <h2>Applied Math</h2>
    <p class="role">Applied mathematicians build and use mathematical models to help answer practical questions.</p>
    <div class="scenario"><strong>Design challenge:</strong> A short ramp rises 3 feet over a horizontal run of 12 feet. The slope is rise ÷ run. Imagine making the ramp twice as long while keeping the same steepness.</div>
    <ol class="steps">
      <li>Calculate the original slope.</li>
      <li>Double the horizontal run. What rise keeps the slope the same?</li>
      <li>What real-world details might a simple slope calculation leave out?</li>
    </ol>
    <div class="formrow">
      <label for="applied-answer">New rise (feet):</label><input type="number" id="applied-answer" placeholder="Your estimate">
      <button class="action" onclick="checkApplied()">Check</button>
    </div>
    <p class="feedback" id="feedback-applied" aria-live="polite"></p>
    <div class="stretch"><strong>Stretch for grades 9–12:</strong> Write the proportional relationship between rise and run. Name one assumption in this model and one additional constraint an engineer might need to consider.</div>
  </section>

  <section class="card panel" id="data" role="tabpanel" hidden>
    <div class="topline"><span class="badge">Make sense of data</span><span class="timer" id="timer-data">05:00</span></div>
    <h2>Statistics &amp; Data Science</h2>
    <p class="role">Statisticians and data scientists look for useful patterns while checking how data was collected and what it can tell us.</p>
    <div class="scenario"><strong>Question:</strong> How long, in minutes, did seven students take to get to school? <strong>Data:</strong> 8, 10, 10, 12, 13, 14, 45</div>
    <ol class="steps">
      <li>Find the mean (average) and the median (middle value).</li>
      <li>Which better describes a “typical” trip here? Why?</li>
      <li>What would you want to know before drawing a conclusion about all students?</li>
    </ol>
    <div class="formrow">
      <label for="data-choice">I think the more typical value is</label>
      <select id="data-choice"><option value="">Choose one</option><option value="mean">the mean</option><option value="median">the median</option></select>
      <button class="action" onclick="checkData()">Check</button>
    </div>
    <p class="feedback" id="feedback-data" aria-live="polite"></p>
    <div class="stretch"><strong>Stretch for grades 9–12:</strong> Calculate both values, then explain how the 45-minute trip affects them differently. Suggest one way to collect a more representative sample.</div>
  </section>
  <p class="footer">When the timer ends, finish your thought: What did you enjoy, and what would you want to investigate next?</p>
</main>
<script>
  const timers = {};
  function startTimer(id) {
    if (timers[id]) clearInterval(timers[id]);
    let left = 300;
    const el = document.getElementById("timer-" + id);
    const tick = () => {
      el.textContent = String(Math.floor(left / 60)).padStart(2,"0") + ":" + String(left % 60).padStart(2,"0");
      if (left <= 0) {
        clearInterval(timers[id]);
        timers[id] = null;
        el.textContent = "Time!";
        return;
      }
      left--;
    };
    tick();
    timers[id] = setInterval(tick, 1000);
  }
  function feedback(id, message, good) {
    const el = document.getElementById("feedback-" + id);
    el.textContent = message;
    el.className = "feedback " + (good ? "good" : "try");
  }
  document.querySelectorAll(".tab").forEach(tab => tab.addEventListener("click", () => {
    document.querySelectorAll(".tab").forEach(t => t.setAttribute("aria-selected", String(t === tab)));
    document.querySelectorAll(".panel").forEach(p => p.hidden = p.id !== tab.dataset.panel);
    startTimer(tab.dataset.panel);
  }));
  function checkTeach() {
    const model = document.getElementById("teach-model").value;
    feedback("teach", "Sample: " + model + " shows 12 as four equal groups of three. Ask: “How could you count all the objects without counting one by one?”", true);
  }
  function checkPure() {
    const value = Number(document.getElementById("pure-answer").value);
    feedback("pure", value === 11 ? "Yes! The differences are 3, 5, 7, 9, then 11. The next square is 36." : "Try subtracting neighboring squares: 4−1, 9−4, 16−9, 25−16. What comes next?", value === 11);
  }
  function checkApplied() {
    const value = Number(document.getElementById("applied-answer").value);
    feedback("applied", value === 6 ? "That keeps the same slope: 3 ÷ 12 = 6 ÷ 24. A real ramp design also needs safety and building requirements." : "If the run doubles from 12 to 24 feet, the rise must double too. Try again.", value === 6);
  }
  function checkData() {
    const value = document.getElementById("data-choice").value;
    feedback("data", value === "median" ? "Good choice: the median is 12 minutes. The 45-minute trip pulls the mean upward. The mean is 16 minutes." : value === "mean" ? "The mean is 16 minutes, but the 45-minute trip pulls it upward. The median is 12. Which seems more typical?" : "Choose mean or median first. Then think about how the 45-minute trip affects the average.", value === "median");
  }
  startTimer("teach");
</script>
</body>
</html>
